messages:
sophie_support: Heads-up — ACME (acme_ops) hit a security/compliance escalation after a key rotation on their on-prem HSM. Post-rotation, signing calls to our KMS started returning CKR_GENERAL_ERROR and we have an audit gap from 02:14–02:18 UTC. Can SRE/KMS own triage? @dan_engineering @matt_prod

acme_ops: confirming. We rotated HSM key via vendor CLI at ~02:12 UTC. After that, client apps saw 500s and some sign ops timed out. We kept the vendor console logs, attaching a snippet here: 

```
2026-03-15T02:13:05Z INFO Key import completed: keyId=redwood-prod-01
2026-03-15T02:14:10Z ERROR sign failed: CKR_GENERAL_ERROR handle=0x7f1a
2026-03-15T02:15:30Z WARN connection reset by peer
```

oncall-kms-bot: alert — 14 KMS session disconnect events between 02:14:00 and 02:18:00 UTC. Collector process restarted at 02:19:22 UTC (auto-restart).

dan_engineering: thanks. First checks: is this CloudHSM or on-prem HSM? acme_ops you said on-prem — which vendor & firmware? Also did you retain HSM audit files locally (/var/log/hsm/audit)?

acme_ops: on-prem vendor: SafeCrypt v3.2.1, FIPS mode ON. We have the /var/log/hsm/audit directory, will upload a tar to the S3 share.

matt_prod: SafeCrypt 3.2.x had a known issue where entropy reseed after key import could block signing for a few seconds and sometimes drop sessions under high concurrency. Could explain the CKR_GENERAL_ERROR + session resets. But the audit gap suggests our collector also missed events.

sophie_support: ok. Action items we need now:
1) acme_ops: upload audit tar and vendor HSM health dump to the S3 share (path in the support ticket).
2) acme_ops: run this quick check on the HSM host and paste output:
```
/usr/bin/pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/safecrypt/libscpkcs11.so -O
ssldebug=$(sudo /opt/safecrypt/bin/hsm_health.sh)
echo "$ssldebug"
```
3) dan_engineering / matt_prod: check our KMS collector logs around 02:12–02:20 UTC for segfaults or restarts.

dan_engineering: looking at our collector logs now — I already see a segmentation fault in the ingestion process at 02:16:21 that caused the collector to crash and restart. Crash log snippet:

```
Mar 15 02:16:21 kms-collector[2345]: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
Mar 15 02:16:21 kms-collector[2345]: goroutine 42 [running]:
Mar 15 02:16:21 kms-collector[2345]: github.com/redwood-inference/kms/collector.(*AuditReader).Read(0xc0000b6000...)
```

dan_engineering: that explains the ingestion gap. However, HSM-side events might still exist on the appliance; we should ask customer to provide native audit logs. If SafeCrypt lost sessions briefly, keys may still be OK, but we need to verify key handles and counters.

matt_prod: mitigations to recommend to customer now (short-term):
- Create a new key (non-destructive), update a single test consumer to point at it, verify sign latency under load.
- Increase HSM session pool / client retry backoff to reduce concurrent session pressure.
- For compliance: collect vendor audit logs + a signed manifest listing files and hashes.

sophie_support: noted. acme_ops — if you can run the pkcs11 object list from the HSM, paste output (sanitized):
```
pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/safecrypt/libscpkcs11.so -O
Objects found: 3
Object 0x7f1a: CKO_PRIVATE_KEY label: "redwood-prod-01"
Object 0x7f1b: CKO_PUBLIC_KEY label: "redwood-prod-01"
```

acme_ops: pasted the output to the ticket. Also uploaded audit tar to s3://redwood-support/acme/1802456789-audit.tar.gz and the vendor health dump to s3://redwood-support/acme/1802456789-health.txt

dan_engineering: downloading now. Quick compliance note: because our collector missed events, for the audit trail we must preserve vendor files and provide a timeline with checksums. I'll create an internal incident and attach the collector crash dump.

sophie_support: I'll open a formal escalation to Security & Compliance and flag for SOC review — need confirmation of no exfil and full integrity of audit files.

matt_prod: RCA suspects: (1) SafeCrypt entropy reseed causing blocking + session resets; (2) our collector crash resulting in ingestion gap. Long-term fixes: vendor patch for SafeCrypt firmware (they have a 3.2.2 candidate), collector hardening (null-pointer guard), and improved replay ingestion so we can backfill missed events.

acme_ops: thank you. ETA on mitigation steps? We can do non-disruptive key onboarding this afternoon if you validate the safe path.

dan_engineering: I can validate the non-disruptive onboarding plan. Steps: create new key, test sign with one app, monitor latency, then cut traffic. I’ll draft step-by-step in the ticket and coordinate a maintenance window.

sophie_support: perfect. For now I’ve added compliance@redwood and vendor-support@safecrypt to the ticket. Will update once we have vendor health analysis and collector fix. :thumbsup:

oncall-kms-bot: escalation created: INC-2026-0421 (priority P2) — assigned to dan_engineering and matt_prod.

acme_ops: appreciate the quick triage — we’ll postpone any further rotations until we get the all-clear.

sophie_support: closing loop for this thread — follow-ups in INC-2026-0421 and the support ticket.
